chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom I had advanced dirhams in exchange for food. When his food was due to me, he sent me the dirhams and said, 'Buy food for yourself and take full satisfaction of your right.' He (the Imam) said, 'I see that you should appoint someone else to do that, or stand with him until he hands over what is yours, and you should not buy it yourself.'

key_terms.اِسْتَوْفِ حَقَّكَ: Take full satisfaction of your right

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for a creditor to receive repayment of a food loan when the debtor returns the money?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific fiqh of 'salaf' (advance payment) for food, ruling that the creditor should avoid personally purchasing the food with the returned cash to prevent ambiguity in the transfer of ownership. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring clear possession (*qabd*) and avoiding *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial transactions, distinguishing between the repayment of the debt and the subsequent acquisition of the commodity.
